# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45 (Bu-Vb Pc45)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc45
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting alone with a woman

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rahonisajja Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 45) governs seclusion between a Buddhist monk and a woman. The rule stipulates that a monk who, seeking privacy, sits in private with a woman commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*). An English translation of the rule and its accompanying analysis is available by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali tradition, it corresponds to rule 45 of the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 126 and its associated Pātimokkha and Parivāra texts. Equivalent rules are preserved across the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga traditions in Sanskrit and Chinese, alongside the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchā*.

 Later Pali reuse appears notably in the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
